chats.answer:
For a family NAS running Audiobookshelf and Calibre-Web, I'd prioritize Docker support, reliability, quiet operation, and easy remote access over raw CPU performance.

Both applications are relatively lightweight. Even with 4–8 family members, you don't need a powerful NAS unless you're also planning to run Plex/Jellyfin, photo management, or other services.

My top recommendation is a 4-bay Intel-based NAS with at least 8 GB RAM and SSD storage for application data. A 2-bay NAS can also work well if your library is modest.

chats.answer:
For a family self-hosting Audiobookshelf and Calibre-Web, I'd recommend a 2-bay or 4-bay NAS with Docker support, an Intel or AMD x86 processor, and at least 4 GB of RAM (preferably 8 GB).

Neither application is particularly demanding. What matters most is reliable storage, easy Docker management, automated backups, and hassle-free access for family members on phones, tablets, and e-readers.

My top choices would be:

Best overall: Synology DS425+ — polished software, simple family administration.

Best value: UGREEN NASync DXP2800 — good hardware for the money.

Best for expansion: UGREEN NASync DXP4800 Plus — more headroom for additional self-hosted services.

I would avoid buying an expensive enterprise NAS just for these two applications. Even with several family members using them simultaneously, a modern entry-level x86 NAS should be plenty.

For the actual storage, I'd start with two 4 TB NAS-rated hard drives in RAID 1, giving roughly 4 TB of usable capacity before filesystem overhead. That is generous for most audiobook and ebook collections. Put Docker application data on an SSD if convenient, but it isn't necessary.

Give each family member their own Audiobookshelf and Calibre-Web login, so reading and listening progress stays separate. Back up the application databases as well as the media files. RAID protects against a drive failure, not accidental deletion.

My recommendation

I'd buy the UGREEN DXP2800 with two mirrored drives unless you specifically want Synology's software ecosystem or expect to expand your storage substantially. It offers more than enough compute power for these applications, with 8 GB RAM out of the box.

One question that would change my recommendation: Will this NAS be exclusively for audiobooks and ebooks, or do you also plan to run Plex/Jellyfin, Immich (photos), Home Assistant, or other self-hosted services?

chats.answer:
For a family NAS running Audiobookshelf and Calibre-Web, I'd prioritize Docker support, reliability, quiet operation, and easy remote access over raw performance.

Both applications are lightweight. You don't need an expensive NAS or a powerful CPU unless you also plan to run Plex/Jellyfin, transcode video, or host many other services.

My top choices are:

Synology DS224+ — best for simplicity and family use.

Synology DS423+ — best for long-term storage expansion.

UGREEN NASync DXP2800 — best value for hardware and performance.

A small Intel N100/N150 mini PC + NAS — best for flexibility and self-hosting control.

For most families, I'd choose a 2-bay NAS with mirrored drives, 8 GB RAM, and Docker Compose support.

Best NAS options in 2026

1. UGREEN NASync DXP2800, 2-Bay NAS with Intel N100 Quad-Core C…

Best overall

Intel N100, 8 GB DDR5, 2.5GbE, NVMe slots. Excellent for Docker and both book servers, with room for additional services.

Synology DSM, Container Manager, established backup tools. Less powerful hardware, with only 2 GB RAM included, but a good choice for simpler administration. 
global.download.synology.com
+1

The older DS224+ and DS423+ are still capable, but I wouldn't prioritize them over current models unless you find a good deal.

Recommended family setup
Each family member gets their own login and reading/listening history.

I'd configure it with two 4 TB NAS-rated CMR drives in RAID 1 (approximately 4 TB usable), Docker Compose, separate application configuration directories, and a scheduled external backup. RAID 1 protects against a single drive failure, not accidental deletion or ransomware.

For remote access, use Tailscale for family devices you control, or a properly secured HTTPS reverse proxy for simpler access without a VPN.

One family-specific detail: check the audiobook clients on everyone's phones, particularly iPhones, before committing to Audiobookshelf.

My choice

UGREEN DXP2800 is the strongest value for these two services. Choose Synology DS225+ if ease of maintenance and its backup ecosystem matter more than hardware performance.

One question that would change my recommendation: Will this NAS be dedicated to audiobooks and ebooks, or will you also store family photos, backups, and movies on it?
